transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-24 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Tara (Halcyon Head of ML), Evan (Halcyon Principal Engineer), Priya (Product), Samir (DevOps)

Summary notes (auto): Quick fidelity audit, two regressions after model bump, fallback drill using quantized variant, security sprint items.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh this is our weekly sync for the Halcyon checkout assistant pilot. Quick agenda — fidelity recap, regression triage, and then a fallback/rollback drill. Marcus, you wanna start with the metric snapshot?
[00:22] Marcus: Yeah sure, um so last week we rolled forward to model-rw-v3, avg token latency is up about 8% on p3 instances, but overall score on the core prompt set dropped from 92.1 to 88.4, so that triggered two clusters of regressions, most of them around product substitution prompts in checkout flows.
[00:41] Evan: Right, the substitutions are bad — like it suggests the wrong SKU code sometimes, which our downstream matcher rejects, so UX gets stuck. We saw a 0.4% increase in checkout fails during the window.
[00:58] Tara: And just to add, a lot of those failing prompts are long-context ones, so maybe the K V cache handling changed? We observed truncated contexts in about 6% of samples.
[01:15] Marcus: Could be, the kv cache alignment was slightly different in the new kernel path. Also we did some more aggressive quantization tests in the canary pipeline which may have altered tokenization boundary handling — so there are two possible causes.
[01:32] Priya: For our success criteria we need under 0.2% checkout fails and mean intent accuracy above 90. We're at 88.4 so we want to decide whether to tune thresholds or roll back.
[01:48] Diego: From Redwood ops perspective, we ran a fallback drill this morning where we served a quantized q4 variant with smaller memory footprint. Latency improved 12% but fidelity dipped further for a specific prompt subset. However the fallback path itself functioned — request routing, canary rollback worked as expected.
[02:07] Samir: Quick ops Q — how do logs get exported for that drill? We need token-level traces and audit logs for compliance.
[02:18] Marcus: Logs were streamed to the staging S3 and audit lines to the control plane; note that the export schema uses "user_id" hashed and we included a sampling flag. We'll share the export script. Small caveat: the KMS handshake during the drill had a transient error once, but rekeying succeeded.
[02:38] Tara: That KMS hiccup worries me, for production we need an HSM-backed KMS and deterministic re-encryption windows.
[02:48] Marcus: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed K M S in the VPC install, and for Hosted we can configure Cloud KMS with enforced rotation. We'll send the KMS guide.
[03:02] Evan: Back to regressions — Marcus, can you walk us through the two clusters and example prompts?
[03:08] Marcus: Sure; cluster A is SKU substitution path — short prompts that ask "Which code for the blue sweater?" and the model returns a similar-but-wrong SKU. Cluster B is multi-step clarifying dialogs where the model drops the last product reference. I have sample transcripts.
[03:27] Tara: We'll upload a 200-sample set for each cluster. Expect us to label golden outputs.
[03:33] Marcus: Great. For mitigation we have three options: 1) tweak scoring thresholds and post-filtering, 2) prompt surgery (explicit SKU anchors), or 3) rollback to v2 while we root cause. The rollback path has the fastest time to resolution but higher ops cost.
[03:55] Priya: If rollback is quick and predictable that's probably our preference for Black Friday-like spikes. But for day-to-day we want fewer false positives.
[04:07] Sofia: Important point — what's the SLO for rollback? Marcus?
[04:11] Marcus: We can do a staged rollback in about 18-24 minutes including traffic drain and warmup on staging-to-prod path, assuming there are no infra hiccups. We captured a 22-min run in rehearsal.
[04:27] Samir: Any impact on in-flight sessions? We need sticky sessions to not break carts.
[04:34] Marcus: We preserve KV cache across instances when we do the redirect if the models are architecture-compatible; otherwise we force a warm restart and advise a lightweight session migration strategy.
[04:49] Evan: You said architecture-compatible — are v3 and v2 compatible for KV?
[04:54] Marcus: Mostly yes, but v3 did change some attention caching offsets which explains the truncated contexts Tara saw. That's likely why cluster B appears.
[05:06] Tara: Ok so I think our immediate play is: run rollback drill on staging, gather log traces, and then either prompt-anchor or patch the scoring.
[05:16] Sofia: Let's run a fallback drill in this meeting — hypothetically — what would be the decision tree?
[05:22] Marcus: Decision tree: if core prompt score < 90 and checkout failure > 0.2% -> immediate staged rollback. Else if score between 90-91 and regressions are in a narrow prompt subset -> prompt-surgery + threshold tweak with monitoring.
[05:39] Priya: For monitoring what thresholds do we set on the score delta and false-positive rate?
[05:44] Marcus: Score delta 1.5 absolute points as a hard trigger, and 0.2% checkout fail rate. We'll instrument near-real-time alerts to Slack and to the Console.
[05:58] Evan: On instrumentation: can we get token-level cost per route? We're trying to model monthly spend.
[06:03] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level breakdown per route and model; Marcus: we'll include a cost snapshot in the rollback drill results.
[06:12] Diego: Small note — we saw slightly different token counts for the quantized variant due to tokenization boundary changes, so cost comparisons need to use normalized tokens.
[06:24] Tara: Security quick-fire: SOC two docs, SSO integration, RBAC for logs, and data residency. We need the SOC2 excerpt and confirmation on log retention windows.
[06:36] Diego: I'll upload the SOC2 summary and the retention policy. For SSO, Redwood supports SAML and OIDC; we can set role mappings. For log retention we can set custom retention in Private, hosted has default 90 days, extendable via archive.
[06:55] Samir: Also want to confirm encryption at rest in S3.
[06:59] Marcus: Yes, server-side encryption with customer-managed keys is supported.
[07:05] Tara: Good. Back to the rollback drill plan — Marcus, what telemetry will you collect?
[07:09] Marcus: Token-level latencies, token counts, per-prompt confidence score, KV cache hit rate, and sample golden comparisons. We'll push artifacts to the shared staging bucket and link in the CRM.
[07:26] Evan: If rollback is 20-25 minutes in rehearsal, what's the customer impact window?
[07:31] Marcus: Worst-case during cutover a small percentage of in-flight sessions might need to re-run a step, but we expect <0.5% user-facing error if sticky session strategy used.
[07:44] Priya: OK let's decide: run the rollback drill on staging, but also start prompt anchors on a small sample for targeted tests.
[07:53] Sofia: Agreed. Who owns the staging run?
[07:56] Marcus: I can own the staging rollback. I'll run it end-to-end and share logs.
[08:02] Tara: We'll push the labeled failing prompts by Friday and mark golden outputs.
[08:09] Sofia: Diego will share SOC2 and KMS docs. I'll follow up with pricing.
[08:14] Marcus: One more note — when we did fallback routing earlier, the decision policy used latency-priority for 10% of traffic; we saw slightly different behavior when traffic was bursty. For production we recommend policy: latency-critical routes go to dedicated low-latency pool, cost-tolerant routes use quantized pool.
[08:35] Evan: That policy mapping makes sense. We'll need per-route mapping in the Console.
[08:40] Marcus: We can provision route mappings and export a CSV of current policy rules.
[08:47] Priya: Does Redwood provide a simulated cost projection if we switch certain routes to Dedicated?
[08:52] Sofia: Yes — I'll run a usage simulation with your pilot metrics and send the projection.
[08:58] Tara: Any final compliance questions?
[09:01] Samir: Just one — are audit exports tamper-evident?
[09:05] Diego: Exports are signed and we can append an HMAC; for Private installs we can forward to a customer audit collector.
[09:15] Evan: Perfect. Any blockers?
[09:18] Tara: None besides getting those failing prompts.
[09:21] Sofia: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[09:25] Diego: I'll attach SOC2/KMS notes to the CRM.
[09:29] Marcus: I'll run the rollback drill on staging by 6/30 and share artifacts.
[09:32] Tara: We'll deliver labeled failures by 6/26.
[09:35] Sofia: I'll send the pricing and simulation by 6/25.
[09:38] Priya: We'll review results next Wed in the same slot.
[09:41] Sofia: Thanks everyone, end meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "KV cache" transcribed sometimes as "K V cash"; "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes shortened to "Redwood Dedi". There were short crosstalk moments between Evan and Tara around 03:00.

Shared artifacts referenced: rollback-runbook.md (link in CRM), sample-failing-prompts.csv (to be uploaded by Halcyon), staging-rollback-logs.zip (to be shared by Marcus).
